name: Mull, Iona & Staffa
tagline: A colourful harbour town, a sacred ancient abbey and a basalt sea cave that once inspired a symphony, all within a short Hebridean hop of each other.
highlight: Stepping inside Fingal's Cave on Staffa, its perfectly hexagonal basalt columns and deep, echoing swell unlike anywhere else on Earth.
shortDescription: A trio of Hebridean islands: Mull's colourful Tobermory harbour, Iona's ancient abbey, and Staffa's extraordinary basalt sea cave.
metaDescription: A Mull, Iona and Staffa travel guide: Tobermory, Iona Abbey, Fingal's Cave, food and how to plan a visit to these Inner Hebridean islands.
knownFor: Tobermory's harbour, Iona Abbey, Fingal's Cave

image.alt: The colourful harbourfront of Tobermory on the Isle of Mull

intro: Mull is the gateway to a trio of Inner Hebridean islands, its main town Tobermory instantly recognisable for the brightly painted buildings lining its small harbour.
A short ferry hop away sits Iona, one of the most spiritually significant places in Scotland, where St Columba founded a monastery in 563 that helped bring Christianity to much of the country.
Further out again is Staffa, home to Fingal's Cave, an extraordinary sea cave of perfectly hexagonal basalt columns that inspired Mendelssohn's Hebrides Overture after his own visit in 1829.

whyVisit.intro: Mull, Iona and Staffa's case rests on combining colourful island character with deep spiritual and natural history.

points.title: Tobermory is one of Scotland's most photogenic towns
points.text: A small harbour lined with brightly painted 18th-century buildings.

points.title: Iona is one of Scotland's most spiritually significant sites
points.text: St Columba's 563 monastery here helped bring Christianity to much of the country.

points.title: Fingal's Cave is unlike anywhere else on Earth
points.text: A sea cave of perfectly hexagonal basalt columns that inspired a famous orchestral overture.

points.title: White-tailed sea eagles are a real, common sighting
points.text: Europe's largest bird of prey, reintroduced to Mull and now thriving.

points.title: It rewards visitors willing to island-hop
points.text: A real sense of remoteness and discovery across three distinct islands.

attractionsIntro: The islands' essential sights combine Tobermory's colour with deep spiritual and natural history further out.

attractions.name: Tobermory's colourful harbour

image.alt: The colourful harbourfront buildings of Tobermory

attractions.text: One of Scotland's most photographed harbours, its 18th-century buildings painted in bright, distinctive colours.
attractions.tip: Arrive by ferry for the best first view of the harbourfront's colours from the water.

attractions.name: Duart Castle

image.alt: Duart Castle on the Isle of Mull

attractions.text: Mull's most dramatic castle, the ancient seat of Clan Maclean on a rocky headland overlooking the Sound of Mull.
attractions.tip: The castle's dungeon and clan history exhibits are worth the extra time inside.

attractions.name: Iona Abbey

image.file: File:Iona Abbey - general view from SW.jpg
image.alt: Iona Abbey on the island of Iona

attractions.text: One of the most spiritually significant sites in Scotland, founded by St Columba in 563 and central to Christianity's spread across the country.
attractions.tip: The short ferry crossing to Iona is worth taking slowly, with views back to Mull.

attractions.name: Fingal's Cave, Staffa

image.alt: Fingal's Cave on the island of Staffa

attractions.text: An extraordinary natural sea cave of perfectly hexagonal basalt columns, its deep swell inspiring Mendelssohn's famous overture.
attractions.tip: Boat trips land on Staffa in calm weather, allowing visitors to walk right into the cave's entrance.

attractions.name: Staffa's basalt columns

image.file: File:Fingal's Cave and basaltic columns, Island of Staffa - geograph.org.uk - 6434394.jpg
image.alt: The hexagonal basalt columns of Staffa

attractions.text: A geological wonder, ancient volcanic activity cooling into thousands of perfectly hexagonal stone columns.
attractions.tip: Puffins nest on Staffa's clifftops in season, an added bonus for visiting boat trips.

attractions.name: Mull's white-tailed sea eagles

image.alt: A white-tailed sea eagle over Mull

attractions.text: A real, thriving population of Europe's largest bird of prey, successfully reintroduced to the island decades ago.
attractions.tip: Dedicated eagle-watching boat trips offer the best chance of a close sighting.

attractions.name: Iona Abbey's cloister

image.file: File:Iona Abbey - view of cloister arcade.jpg
image.alt: The cloister arcade at Iona Abbey

attractions.text: A peaceful, restored medieval cloister, still home to an active religious community today.
attractions.tip: The abbey remains a working spiritual community, worth visiting with quiet respect.

thingsToDoIntro: The islands reward slow, unhurried travel, whether by ferry, boat trip or on foot.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Tobermory's harbourfront

image.alt: The main street along Tobermory's harbourfront

thingsToDo.text: A relaxed way to spend a morning, browsing shops and cafés along the colourful harbour.
thingsToDo.tip: A good base for arranging boat trips out to Staffa and Iona.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Duart Castle

image.file: File:Duart Castle, Isle of Mull - geograph.org.uk - 3311258.jpg
image.alt: Touring Duart Castle on the Isle of Mull

thingsToDo.text: A worthwhile hour or two, exploring the ancient seat of Clan Maclean on its dramatic headland.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine with the castle's tea room for a break with a sea view.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Iona Abbey

image.file: File:Iona Abbey - view of abbey and replica carved stone.jpg
image.alt: Visiting Iona Abbey on the island of Iona

thingsToDo.text: A reflective few hours, exploring one of Scotland's most spiritually significant sites in real depth.
thingsToDo.tip: Allow time for the short walk around the wider island, not just the abbey itself.

thingsToDo.title: Boat to Fingal's Cave

image.alt: A boat trip to Fingal's Cave on Staffa

thingsToDo.text: A memorable half-day trip, weather permitting, landing on Staffa to walk right into the famous cave.
thingsToDo.tip: Book ahead in summer, and stay flexible — trips depend entirely on sea conditions.

thingsToDo.title: Spot white-tailed sea eagles

image.alt: A white-tailed sea eagle spotted on Mull

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding wildlife experience, with real, reliable chances of spotting Europe's largest bird of prey.
thingsToDo.tip: Dedicated eagle-watching boat trips depart regularly from Tobermory in season.

thingsToDo.title: Sample Tobermory cheese

image.file: File:20150125 Tobermory, Isle of Mull Cheese - Der Schweizer - WikiLovesCheese Vienna 8919.jpg
image.alt: Tobermory cheese made on the Isle of Mull

thingsToDo.text: A worthwhile stop at a local farm producing distinctive cheese from Mull's own dairy herds.
thingsToDo.tip: Check opening hours for farm shop visits and tastings.

foodIntro: Food across the islands leans on fresh seafood and Mull's own dairy and whisky traditions.

foods.name: Tobermory cheese

image.file: File:2015-01-25 Tobermory, Isle of Mull Cheese Sgriob-ruadh Farm - hu - 7901.jpg
image.alt: Cheese made at a farm near Tobermory

foods.text: Distinctive artisan cheese made from the island's own dairy herds, a real point of local pride.
foods.whereToTry: Farm shops and delis throughout Tobermory.

foods.name: Fresh langoustines
foods.text: A Hebridean specialty, sweet shellfish landed straight from the surrounding waters.

foods.name: Tobermory whisky
foods.text: Mull's own distillery product, made right on the harbourfront since 1798.
foods.whereToTry: The distillery itself, and pubs throughout Tobermory.

foods.name: Haggis, neeps and tatties

image.alt: Haggis served with neeps and tatties, Scotland's national dish

foods.text: A warming meal after a day of island-hopping or a boat trip to Staffa.

foods.name: Cullen skink

image.alt: Cullen skink, a traditional Scottish smoked haddock soup

foods.text: A welcome, warming choice after a breezy boat trip out to Staffa or Iona.

foods.name: Scottish shortbread
foods.text: A simple, buttery treat, good provisions for a day of ferry crossings and boat trips.

accommodation.intro: Tobermory serves as the islands' main base, small but well set up for travellers.

areas.name: Tobermory
areas.bestFor: Being central to boat trips and ferry connections
areas.text: The most practical base, with the widest choice of guesthouses and restaurants.

areas.name: Elsewhere on Mull
areas.text: Smaller villages around the island offer real solitude away from Tobermory's harbour.

options.detail: Weather-dependent, so build flexibility into any itinerary.

gettingAround.intro: A car helps on Mull itself, while Iona is small enough to explore entirely on foot.

options.text: Useful for reaching Duart Castle and Fionnphort for the Iona ferry.
options.detail: Roads on Mull are narrow and largely single-track.

options.text: The only way to explore the small island once you arrive.

options.detail: Widely available from Tobermory, Fionnphort and Iona.

bestTime.headline: May to September for the best weather and boat trip reliability
bestTime.summary: The islands are visitable through the warmer months, with far fewer boat sailings and services outside the main season.

seasons.text: Mild weather with good odds of calm seas for boat trips to Staffa.
The busiest season, with the widest choice of ferry and boat trip sailings.
A quieter window with still-decent weather odds.

bestTime.avoid: Booking a rigid winter Staffa boat trip — check conditions closely, since sailings are entirely weather-dependent.

days.title: Iona and Staffa

days.morning: Ferry to Iona and visit the abbey.
days.afternoon: Boat trip to Staffa and Fingal's Cave.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Mull, Iona and Staffa visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book ferry crossings to Mull ahead in summer, especially for a car.
Check Staffa boat trip conditions closely — sailings depend entirely on weather.
Build flexible days into your itinerary in case of cancelled crossings.
Pack a proper waterproof layer regardless of season — the islands are exposed.
Bring binoculars for the best chance of spotting sea eagles.
Respect Iona Abbey's status as an active religious community during your visit.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Mull, Iona and Staffa?
faq.a: Two days covers Tobermory, Duart Castle, Iona and a Staffa boat trip comfortably.

faq.q: Can you visit Staffa without a private boat?
faq.a: Yes — regular organised boat trips run from Mull, Iona and Oban, weather permitting.

faq.q: Is Iona Abbey still a working religious site?
faq.a: Yes — it remains home to an active spiritual community, alongside its role as a historic visitor attraction.

faq.q: What is Fingal's Cave known for?
faq.a: Its perfectly hexagonal basalt columns and deep, echoing acoustics, which inspired Mendelssohn's Hebrides Overture.

faq.q: Can you see sea eagles on Mull?
faq.a: Yes — Mull has one of Britain's best populations of white-tailed sea eagles, reintroduced decades ago and now thriving.

faq.q: Do you need a car on these islands?
faq.a: Helpful on Mull itself, though Iona is small enough to explore entirely on foot once you arrive.
